lead: somebody drove three hours to look at it, stayed until the light went, thanked you and left, and at no point in that afternoon did the conversation come round to you.
sun: a stranger can have the whole of it in an afternoon — how it was done, what the difficult part was, what you were after — because it went out the only way anything of yours goes: finished, admired, nothing withheld. so the question that would otherwise arrive next, about the person who made it, is answered by the object, wrongly, and closed.
moon: no cover was ever built here. the one you have assembled itself out of the work being absorbing enough to take up a room's whole attention, and it rests on that single upright, and it has held thirty years unmaintained. under it is everything nobody has thought to ask: which pieces you cannot look at, what you make of the people who admire them, the year you nearly stopped.
pull: you are the most looked-at person you know and the least asked-after, and the thing keeping the rest of you out of view is the same thing bringing everybody to the door.
tension: a guest works out late in the evening that she has done all the talking, apologises warmly, and that apology is the nearest thing to an enquiry you have had in years. people call it privacy and mean it kindly. nothing about it was chosen. and one upright holds it all, so a thin decade takes the cover off in a season and leaves someone with no practice at being looked at standing where the object was.
cost: a room will stay with your work for three hours and go home satisfied, and not much made by anyone manages that. the same object is doing a second job nobody specified, and it was never inspected for that one, because a shelter you did not put up is not a shelter you check. it comes down whenever the work does, at whatever age that turns out to be.

lead: the method is available to anybody who asks for it. the house is not, and both answers come out of the same person inside the same week, and whoever gets the second one cannot make it fit the other.
sun: the design, the way of getting the difficult part right, all of it is out, attributed, and had for the asking. nothing of yours has gone out with a condition on it, and the thought of putting one there has not arrived. so everything of yours that could be reached has been reached, none of it is held against anybody, and there is exactly one place where the answer has ever been no.
moon: one line got drawn, once, and has not been redrawn since. who is inside, what gets decided here, which evenings are not available — settled early, and it holds whether or not you are having a good year. nobody living there has needed defending by you. that boundary is the only one you ever set, and it went round four people and not round anything you made.
pull: four people live inside the single refusal of your life. everything else you made is in the open with no rule on it at all, and neither of those has been explained to anybody.
tension: your daughter asked to bring one of them to dinner, someone decent who has worked off your method for years, and you said no without a reason, because the rule has never had a reason attached. she read it as snobbery and has not asked again. nothing indoors has ever been explained: a line that held before any of them was born does not present as a decision somebody made, it presents as the shape of a house.
cost: the trade moves faster near you than anywhere else, because nothing leaving your hands has ever needed watching, and the people indoors have never had to share you with it. the exposure lands in one place. every year the household stays sound is a year the work stood out there under your name with nobody minding it, and the quiet indoors is paid for out of that.

lead: she had it finished for four months and could not tell, and it was you who said now, it is done, put it out. six people can name the week you did that for them.
sun: you have never held a finished thing for a season to see how you felt about it. it is done, so it goes, complete, under your name, into whatever room will take it. they do not come to you for an opinion on quality; they can see quality, most of them better than they admit. what stops them is the letting go, a motion nobody ever had to teach you.
moon: so you take them the rest of the way. the last stretch — the week of nearly, the fourth revision that is really a delay — is where you walk beside somebody, patiently and expertly, and it ends at the hour the thing goes out with their name on it. what happens to a made thing afterwards is the country on the other side, and you have no directions.
pull: a dozen people got their best work into the open because you walked them the last stretch. the far side was never mentioned. nothing in you has ever needed to hear about it.
tension: one of them had his lifted eighteen months later by a firm with a legal department, and he came to you first, because you are why it was ever out there. you had nothing for him. no clause you had ever used, no arrangement, no name of anybody who handles this — the apparatus is missing from you, and missing because the lack has never registered. he was polite about it. he still asks whether the next one is ready.
cost: nobody else gets them across. the ones who talk a person into publishing usually have something riding on it, and you visibly have nothing, which is why a word from you moves someone who has not moved in a year. where you deliver them is the open ground you have stood on your whole life without cover. they arrive on your say-so, and they arrive unarmed, the way you did.

lead: you finish things and they are gone inside the month, bare and admired and yours by name. the exception is the one you and she have been going to make since you were both twenty-six.
sun: forty of them went the same way: right on the thursday, gone by the monday, no terms on any of it and nothing kept in a drawer against a bad year. so the ordinary account of a thing left unfinished for twenty-two years — that you are afraid of it being seen, or afraid it is not good — describes nothing here. no piece of yours has ever been held out of the light.
moon: holding is the far end of you, and it stands a long way off — fourteen stations, either way round, and no two stations on this wheel stand further apart. nothing on the road between them answers to both. so what runs between you and her sits where nothing you know about finishing can reach it. she pulls, you pull, and no date has ever been named.
pull: you have handed over the best things you made the week they were done, and the one you cannot finish is the one you could not survive letting go of. those two have never met.
tension: twenty-two years of next year has a shape to it from outside. her husband thinks you are stringing her along; two people who love you both have privately settled on an affair that never happened. the true account persuades nobody, because all of them have watched you release work you cared about far more than this, cheerfully, in a week, and start the next one. the evidence is on their side and it is good evidence.
cost: nothing gets stuck with you. a thing is right, it is gone, the next one starts, a rate almost nobody sustains and why there is so much of it. the one you hold is pulled from both ends and has no finish. when either of you lets go it will not be left as work: a dropped line stops existing, and neither of you could name what had gone.
